galleries.name: Carlos/Ishikawa
galleries.note: Oscar Murillo presented work here in 2011. Issy Wood held a solo show here in 2017.

tierAssessment.reason: 1 eligible entrants across the three years. At least 10 are required.

programmeAudit.summary: All three presenting programmes were reconciled with their offsite and guest credits. Rose Salane was the sole eligible entrant in 2018–20 and subsequently exhibited at MIT and the Whitney. One artist is below the ten-artist tier minimum.

galleries.name: Arcadia Missa
galleries.note: Jesse Darling and Nnena Kalu exhibited here before winning the Turner Prize.

programmeAudit.summary: The London index omits at least one presenting-gallery exhibition in New York. Each group show and exchange needs named participant checks, and a museum outcome alone does not establish an eligible debut.

galleries.name: Emalin
galleries.note: The gallery shows at the Clerk’s House in Shoreditch and at Helmet Row. Its programme includes Alvaro Barrington.

artists.name: Kris Lemsalu Malone & Kyp Malone Lemsalu

tierAssessment.reason: 2 eligible entrants across the three years. At least 10 are required.

rowResults.name: Kris Lemsalu Malone & Kyp Malone Lemsalu

programmeAudit.summary: The three programme censuses identify zero eligible entrants in 2018, two in 2019 and zero in 2020. Both entrants were collaborative practices. One has a verified museum exhibition in the five-year window and the other has unresolved follow-up. Two entrants fall below the minimum of ten.

galleries.name: Soft Opening
galleries.note: Its London programme includes Maren Karlson, Rhea Dillon and Tenant of Culture.

outcomes.organization: San Francisco Museum of Modern Art

programmeAudit.summary: The exhibition archive lists 36 openings across both London spaces. Four group checklists add artists missing from the archive headlines. Documented institutional trajectories exist, while several early career histories and repeat appearances still need reconciliation.

galleries.name: Ginny on Frederick
galleries.note: Its Frieze presentation with Jack O’Brien led to a Camden Art Centre commission.

programmeAudit.summary: The gallery preserves the archive of Ginny’s itinerant programme. It includes exhibitions in Wales, London, Leipzig and Italy before the later permanent London space. Several artist baselines and the status of guest-led projects remain unresolved.

galleries.name: Brunette Coleman
galleries.note: Presented Nat Faulkner at Frieze London, where he won the 2024 Camden Art Centre Emerging Artist Prize.

tierAssessment.reason: 0 eligible entrants across the three years. At least 10 are required.

programmeAudit.summary: Brunette Coleman was founded in 2023. Its archive includes an off-site exhibition that February. All three audited years predate the programme and contain zero eligible entrants.

galleries.name: Rose Easton
galleries.note: Opened in 2021. Its artist roster includes Tasneem Sarkez, Eva Gold and Jan Gatewood.

tierAssessment.reason: 0 eligible entrants across the three years. At least 10 are required.

programmeAudit.summary: Rose Easton dates its launch, including its earlier name Moarain House, to October 2021. All three years have a verified count of zero eligible entrants. A rate requires a cohort of artists.

galleries.name: OOF Gallery
galleries.note: Its football-focused exhibition programme has a permanent home at Warmington House beside Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

programmeAudit.summary: OOF presented exhibitions across London before its permanent space opened in 2021. Four guest-venue projects are documented here. Lydia Blakeley went on to exhibit at the Hayward Gallery. A complete annual guest programme and several early artist histories are still missing.

galleries.name: 47 Canal
galleries.note: The gallery’s roster includes Ajay Kurian, Danielle Dean and Anicka Yi.

programmeAudit.summary: 47 Canal showed Emmanuel Louisnord Desir in 2020 before his Hammer Museum exhibition in 2023. Earlier gallery credits and professional debuts remain open for other artists in the exhibitions and exchanges, including José López Serra.

galleries.name: Kraupa-Tuskany Zeidler
galleries.note: The Berlin programme includes Anna Uddenberg’s solo shows in 2017 and 2021.

programmeAudit.summary: The Berlin archive lists twelve exhibitions, with two additional co-organised programmes in Munich and at Wilhelmhallen. The 2020 census yields zero entrants. Three baseline cases remain open in 2018 and one in 2019. Even if all four qualified, the documented programme would fall below the ten-entrant minimum.

galleries.name: blank projects
galleries.note: Founded as a project space in 2005, the gallery became commercial in 2012 and shows artists from the region and its diaspora.

programmeAudit.summary: The gallery archive records 23 openings across the three calendar years, including a co-presentation in Berlin. Natalie Paneng reached Torrance Art Museum within five years. Earlier university purchases and ambiguous event dates affect other apparently strong candidates.

galleries.name: Harper’s
galleries.note: Fernandez first showed at Harper’s Apartment in 2018. By 2024 the gallery had mounted three solo exhibitions of his work.

outcomes.organization: Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art Africa
Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art Africa

programmeAudit.summary: The multi-location archive yields 37 openings at East Hampton, Harper’s Apartment and Chelsea. Brutus and Namoda reached Zeitz MOCAA and Dal-Pra reached the Musée d’Orsay within five years. In 2019, 13 of 14 named artists were returning or had longer careers. The classification of Bialke’s early record and several group-show participants in the other years keep the denominator open.

events.title: An early show at Carlos/Ishikawa
events.detail: The artist’s CV records animals die from eating too much – bingo! in London.

events.title: Joins David Zwirner
events.detail: David Zwirner dates its representation of Murillo to September 2013.

events.title: Solo exhibition at South London Gallery
events.detail: The London institution opened its exhibition of Murillo’s paintings and installation.

events.title: A Mercantile Novel
events.detail: Murillo’s first exhibition with David Zwirner brought a working candy factory to the New York gallery.

events.title: Shares the Turner Prize
events.detail: Murillo was one of four joint winners of the 2019 Turner Prize.

events.title: The flooded garden at Tate Modern
events.detail: Visitors helped make a large-scale painting in the Turbine Hall.

events.title: Unfinished thinking opens in Paris
events.detail: David Zwirner presented paintings from Murillo’s manifestation series alongside his Social Maps.

events.title: When You I Feel
events.detail: Carlos/Ishikawa presented Wood’s solo show in London.

events.title: All The Rage at Goldsmiths CCA
events.detail: Four galleries brought together paintings drawn from auction catalogues, snapshots and everyday objects.

events.title: Study For No at Lafayette Anticipations
events.detail: Wood’s first French solo exhibition brought more than 60 paintings to Paris.

events.title: Stockholm Syndrome and Other System Failures
events.detail: Arcadia Missa records this London presentation in Darling’s exhibition history.

events.title: The Great Near
events.detail: Solo presentation at Arcadia Missa in London.

events.title: The Ballad of Saint Jerome at Tate Britain
events.detail: Darling presented the exhibition in Tate Britain’s Art Now programme.

events.title: Wins the Turner Prize
events.detail: Tate named Darling the 2023 winner in Eastbourne. His nominations included exhibitions at Modern Art Oxford and Camden Art Centre.

events.title: On Our Knees
events.detail: Arcadia Missa presented a new solo exhibition of Darling’s work in London.

events.title: First London commercial solo show
events.detail: Arcadia Missa exhibited Kalu’s hanging sculptures and drawings. ActionSpace identifies this as her first commercial solo exhibition in the city.

events.title: Hanging sculptures at Manifesta 15
events.detail: Kalu’s Barcelona installation was one of the presentations cited in her Turner Prize nomination.

events.title: Arcadia Missa announces representation
events.detail: ActionSpace announced the gallery would represent Kalu following her 2024 solo show.

events.title: Wins the Turner Prize
events.detail: The award was announced in Bradford following Kalu’s exhibitions in Barcelona and Liverpool.

events.title: Albedo at Brunette Coleman
events.detail: Faulkner’s solo exhibition ran through 14 September in London.

events.title: Camden Art Centre Emerging Artist Prize
events.detail: Faulkner won the prize for his presentation with Brunette Coleman in the Focus section of Frieze London.

events.title: Strong water at Camden Art Centre
events.detail: Faulkner’s first major UK institutional exhibition occupied Camden’s Central Space and Gallery 3.

events.title: Waiting For The Sun To Kill Me
events.detail: Ginny on Frederick hosted this early London exhibition.

events.title: Camden Art Centre Emerging Artist Prize
events.detail: The award recognised O’Brien’s presentation with Ginny on Frederick at Frieze London.

events.title: The Reward at Camden Art Centre
events.detail: A new commission filled Gallery Three following O’Brien’s Frieze prize.

events.title: Trip at Brunette Coleman
events.detail: The gallery’s solo presentation ran until 31 October.

events.title: LAG at Soft Opening
events.detail: The London gallery presented a solo exhibition at its Minerva Street space.

events.title: White-Knuckle in London
events.detail: Rose Easton records the show in its exhibition history for Sarkez.

events.title: Childermass at the Whitney Biennial
events.detail: The Whitney installed Kurian’s sculpture in its 2017 biennial, crediting 47 Canal.

events.title: BIG BABY in Berlin
events.detail: Kraupa-Tuskany Zeidler presented Uddenberg’s solo show during Gallery Weekend Berlin.
